name: Transport Phenomena: Gradivane
subtitle: Transport Phenomena Course
shortDescription: Learn transport phenomena by building: size a pin fin, plan a drug patch, pick a catalyst pellet. Adaptive quizzes and seven cited labs. Free core course.
longDescription:
Transport Phenomena: Gradivane is a course app for engineering undergraduates that teaches how momentum, heat and mass move, and what the three have in common.

Learn it two ways and switch at any time. Classical follows the usual syllabus order across 29 units: fluxes and the three laws, shell balances for Couette and tube flow, power-law fluids, boundary layers, conduction and fins, transient conduction, laminar convection, diffusion, diffusion with reaction, and convective mass transfer with the Chilton-Colburn analogy. Real-world starts from something you want to make, and the theory appears at the moment you need it: design a heat-sink pin fin, plan a drug-delivery patch, size a catalyst pellet, pump a shear-thinning polymer. Finished designs are saved on your Made-it shelf.

Seven interactive labs, each tied to a cited relation and checked against a second numerical method: a boundary-layer studio with Blasius profiles and thermal layers, a space-time map of a cooling slab, a fin bench, tube-flow rheology for Newtonian and power-law fluids, a catalyst pellet with the Thiele modulus, an analogy explorer for Prandtl and Schmidt numbers, and an erfc penetration front.

Adaptive practice: 1019 original questions across four levels from Beginner to Research: 345 with numeric answers and 674 multiple choice. Numeric answers are accepted within a tolerance and every numeric answer is cross-checked by a separate numerical solver. Your mastery is tracked on the device for each concept, fades gently when you are away, and decides what is suggested next. After every quiz you get encouraging, specific feedback with links to the lesson, the lab and a free drill for what to look at next. Choose 5, 10, 20, 40 or a custom number of questions, or take a timed mock exam.

Sources are cited and open in a full-width sheet with Back and Close. Text size goes from 50 to 300 percent on every screen. The app works offline and keeps your progress on the device.

Free: 4 of the 7 labs (boundary-layer studio, transient slab field, tube-flow rheology cutaway, fin heat-sink bench), 9 of the 17 builds, the first full mock paper, levels 1 and 2, and quiz lengths of 5 and 10. One optional monthly subscription, Gradivane Plus Monthly, adds the other 3 labs (catalyst pellet, penetration front, analogy explorer), the other 8 builds, the Advanced and Research levels, and quiz lengths of 20, 40 or your own number. Lessons, worked solutions and your progress always stay free. Billing is one plain monthly price, shown by the store before you confirm and charged to your store account. The subscription renews every month until you cancel it in the App Store or Google Play subscription settings, at any time. A cancellation takes effect when the paid month ends: Plus stays on until then, you pay for that month only and nothing is pro-rated. Refund requests are handled by Apple or Google. Restore purchases is in More.

Education only: examples use idealised models and are not a design standard for real equipment. Not affiliated with any university or textbook publisher named in the sources.
